Name: Murmur of Bees
Author: HarrisonGrey
Description:
[center]Ever wanted the Bee Houses to feel more like you were taking care of real, live animals? Ever wanted to take care of different types of bees? Introducing [b]Murmur of Bees[/b], a Bee House overhaul meant to add depth and variety to the Bee Houses of Stardew Valley![/center]
﻿Taking influence from the fetch quests of the Fish Ponds while respecting the self-reliant nature of the vanilla bee houses, this mod gives you the ability to periodically give gifts to your bees which can increase their capabilities. These capabilities come in three levels; [i]First[/i], bee houses placed on the farm are initially empty and you must first place a Queen Bee (purchasable at Marnie's) in one to start your hive, which then behaves like the vanilla bee houses (one honey, wild or flower flavored, per bee house every four days). [b]All bee houses in an area count towards the same hive, so only one Queen is needed to cover the whole farm.[/b]  [i]Second[/i], an established hive can be given a gift which will determine which kind of bees they become, with each bee producing their honey a little bit differently (for example, Bumblebees make higher quality honey, while Honey Bees make honey more frequently). [i]Finally[/i], as with most farm animals, gifting your bees a Golden Animal Cracker will make them even more productive; they might even feel comfortable enough to produce Queens you can save and use to start your hive again the following year.
﻿But that's just the bees on your farm; leave a bee house anywhere else in the valley and wild bees will automatically inhabit it.  Wild bees may also be given gifts to increase their productivity, though they will not accept the Golden Animal Crackers.  Bee houses placed on Ginger Island also behave a bit differently; they will need a Queen to get their hive started, though they are hardy and need no extra gifts. The challenge is finding the Queen in this tropical environment; you can't just take a bee from the mainland and put it on your island, you'll need to find a native species. All bee houses within one of these areas (on the farm, outside the farm, and on Ginger Island) behave as one hive, so bee houses do not need to be upgraded individually, gifts given to any bee house within one of those areas counts towards them all in that area.
﻿Bees will not accept gifts at any time, but will signal to you through a visual and aural signifier that they're ready to receive a gift (not counting empty bee houses, you can place a Queen Bee in an empty bee house any time and it does not display a signifier).  Keep an eye out for the sight of bees swarming outside your bee houses or for the sound of bees buzzing to know when you can give them a gift to take them to the next stage in their development.
﻿As with real life bees and in the base game, Winter is a period of hibernation for the bees; bees will not produce during Winter, and by Spring your hive will reset and need you to start over. You can use this opportunity to try and get a new species of bee or you can use a Queen you kept from your previous year to jump your hive immediately to the second stage. Bees are also temperamental about their environment; if they received a [i]Wilted Bouquet[/i], your farm hive might up and leave, giving you the opportunity to start over on their development.  Bees outside the farm also stop producing during Winter and reset in Spring, though they do not respond to the Wilted Bouquet; Ginger Island bees produce all through Winter, but still reset in Spring.

[b]The Hive[/b]
﻿Your Hive is started as soon as you add a Queen Bee to a bee house, but importantly the Hive exists independent of individual bee houses. This means that if you place a Queen Bee into a bee house on the farm then pick up the bee house, the Hive is still active. Adding new bee houses adds them to the existing Hive. Any changes made to the Hive (adding a Queen, upgrading with a gift, resetting it with a Wilted Bouquet) apply to the whole Hive, not just individual bee houses.  This means that to start your hive across all bee houses on your farm, you only need one Queen to cover the whole area, not one Queen per bee house.
﻿There are three possible hives at a time, covering specific areas; the [b]Farm[/b], including all outdoors locations and the Greenhouse (where you can ultimately choose between specific bee species as detailed in the next section); the whole of [b]Ginger Island[/b] (which has its own unique bee species); and [b]all areas outside the farm[/b] which count as one big area for bee purposes, where you can find Wild Bees. Changes made to a single bee house in any of these areas affect all bee houses in that whole area. 
[b]
The Bees
[/b]  ﻿Both wild bees and ungifted bees in your farm behave as the bees in the base game, but giving your farm bees a gift will change them into a specific species of bee, all of which behave differently and have a unique Bee House sprite.  Your options are:

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1303/67153256-1757368484.png[/img]﻿
﻿[i]﻿Honey Bees[/i]: Honey bees are domestic bees that have been crossbred for maximal honey production; they produce honey every 3 days instead of 4, and sometimes as frequently as 2 days once they've received a Golden Animal Cracker. The hive still acts in unison, so if you sync their harvest, they'll all produce on the same day next time.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1303/67153256-1757368587.png[/img]
﻿[i]Bumblebees[/i]: Bumblebees are bigger and produce higher quality, Silver and Gold star honey; they can produce Iridium star honey once they've received a Golden Animal Cracker.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1303/67153256-1757368641.png[/img]
﻿[i]Wasps[/i]: Did you know some species of wasp actually produce honey? They do, though these wasps aren't the best honey producers; they produce Wasp Honey every 7 days, which has a price boost of 200g but is not flavored by nearby flowers. However, they make up for their lack of honey production by being an excellent natural pest control; when you have a colony of wasps in your bee houses, you will have a permanent buff (+2 Farming) when outdoors on your farm. If given a Golden Animal Cracker, the wasps give you an even better buff (+3 Farming and +2 Luck).

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1303/67153256-1757368708.png[/img]
[i]﻿Mason Bees (Only available if you have [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/36832]my Perfumery Mod[/url])[/i]: Mason Bees are solitary bees who bring flowers back to their nests to feed their larva; this means they do not produce honey, but produce Mixed Flower Seeds and Dried Flowers instead. Give them a Golden Animal Cracker, and they'll produce Perfume as well.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1303/67153256-1757368811.png[/img]﻿
﻿[i]Wild Bees[/i]: Any bee houses outside the farm are automatically inhabited by Wild Bees; Wild Bees can receive gifts and be upgraded, though they cannot be turned into any other kind of bee.  As they are upgraded, they produce more honey at a time, up to 4 a stack.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1303/67153256-1757368762.png[/img]﻿
[i]﻿Ginger Island Bees[/i]: The native bees of Ginger Island are hardy enough once they get their hive started that they don't need any more gifts or upgrades; they work through the Winter and flowers on Ginger Island stick around all year and out of season. Their honey is purple and has a small price boost of 150g.

﻿What items do you need to give your bees in order to get each type? That's a puzzle you'll need to figure out, but you can get some help by asking around. Some people in the Valley have more information about bees, namely animal experts like Marnie, scientists like Demetrius or Maru, kids who love bugs like Vincent or their schoolteachers like Penny.  For anyone who just wants the answers:
[spoiler]Fruit gives you Honey Bees, Syrups give you Bumblebees, Bug Meat gives you Wasps, Flowers give you Mason Bees. Foraging items can be given to Wild Bees twice for two extra levels of upgrades.  Bee houses won't accept another gift for 10 days after the last one.[/spoiler]

﻿In their final upgrade, all versions of the bee house will occasionally give you Queen Bees.  Wild bees will give the regular Queen Bee item (so you can technically get through this whole process without ever buying any from the store), while bee houses on the farm will give Queen Bees of whatever species they're currently set to.  Because Queen Bees are delicate, living creatures, they cannot be thrown away or shipped, but they can be sold to both Marnie and Pierre in person. Island Bee Queens, because they are not native to the Valley, cannot be sold to Marnie or Pierre, but can be traded to the Island Trader.

[b]More Bee Produce[/b]
﻿In addition to honey, bees can produce a few other things, namely Honeycomb and (if you have certain other mods) Beeswax.  Honeycomb is a sweet snack that can be eaten to gain health and energy.  Beeswax is only available if you have either [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/30597]Bees Plus[/url] or [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/24842]Cornucopia[/url]﻿; both mods include their own versions of Beeswax as an item, and a Wax Station or Wax Barrel machine that can process Beeswax into other goods. Since both mods do more or less the same thing, most players are likely to choose one or the other, but bees can produce both types of Beeswax if both mods are installed.
﻿Wasps and Mason Bees do not produce Honeycomb or Beeswax; Wasps instead may occasionally produce Bug Meat in stacks of 1-3 and rarely Bug Steak. Mason Bees produce Mixed Flower Seeds as their default item, but can also produce Dried Flowers.  If you have Cornucopia installed, the Mason Bees will produce the Dried Flowers from that mod; if you do not have Cornucopia installed, Mason Bees can still produce Dried Flowers added by this mod.  Dried Flowers from this mod can also be produced by the Dehydrator by processing a stack of 3 flowers.  Dried Flowers will only be added by this mod if you do not have Cornucopia.
﻿Bee gift items, specifically the Honeycomb and Dried Flowers from this mod, can be used in the Sewing Machine to create two new Bee Hood hats. Honeycomb or Dried Flowers with Cloth will get you the Bee Hood, while the same two items used with Wool will get you the Medieval Bee Hood.

[b]Honey Price Can Affect Mead[/b]
﻿Inspired by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/22848]Better Honey Mead[/url], this mod can be configured to allow the price of honey to affect the price of the mead it processes into; this is calculated at a rate of 1.5x the price of the honey, plus another 150g. This means Wild Honey results in Mead worth 300g like usual, but higher priced honey, either by flowers or by Wasp Honey or Wild Honey from Ginger Island, will be worth more.
﻿This feature is like a truncated version of what's available with Better Honey Mead; while the price boost is the same, one thing I could not replicate in a satisfactory way is the Mead keeping the name of the flower; to get that feature, you can use BHM in addition to this mod. Keep in mind, BHM colors its Honey and Mead based on the color of the flowers used; you might want to use my feature [i]instead of BHM[/i] if you like the more natural colors of honey and mead found in my mod versus the flower colored sprites in BHM.
﻿[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/39814]Simple Flower Mead[/url] similarly keeps the name of the flower in flower-flavored Mead but doesn't affect the sprite at all; it can also be used in addition to this mod.
﻿The Mead price boost and the additional bee produce items are configurable in...

[b]The Config Options[/b]
﻿There are a few things that can be configured or disabled by this mod, starting with:

"﻿[i]Bee Gifts[/i]": Your options are "true" or "false"; this determines whether or not the additional items listed in More Bee Produce will be produced by the bees; disabling this feature prevents Honeycomb from being added as an item, Beeswax from being produced, the wasps from producing Bug Meat and Bug Steak, and Mason Bees from producing Dried Flowers from either this mod or Cornucopia.  Mason Bees will still produce Perfume and Mixed Flower Seeds, as those are their main produce instead of honey.
﻿"[i]Bee Gift Chance[/i]": Configures how frequently bees produce their additional produce items.  Defaults to 20% of the time. This does not change how frequently they produce Queens.
﻿"[i]Dried Flowers[/i]": If you do not have Cornucopia, this lets you configure the Dried Flowers item added by this mod; you can disable them entirely, add them to be produced by both the Mason Bees and the Dehydrator, or just produced by the Mason Bees but not the Dehydrator (to avoid interference with other mods that add flower options to the Dehydrator).
﻿"[i]Honeycomb[/i]": This can disable whether Honeycomb as an item is added by this mod.  It will not be added as an object or produced by any bees.

﻿"[i]Bee Sound[/i]": A custom sound of bees is added for when Bee Houses receive an item or as an aural signifier that a Bee House is ready to receive an item. This sound can be disabled; Bee Houses will make no sound when ready (a visual signifier will still play), and will use the standard "Ship" sound when given an item.
﻿"[i]Wasp Buff Greenhouse[/i]": Whether the Wasp Buff is applied to inside the Greenhouse. This only works if you also have Better Beehouses installed, see Compatibility below for more details.
﻿"[i]Mead Price Boost[/i]": Whether or not this mod factors the price of the honey into the price of mead made with it. Turns off automatically if you have Better Honey Mead installed. By default this is turned off.
﻿"[i]Empty Beehouse[/i]": Default true. If you have the Better Beehouse bee particles turned on, the bees won't appear when the Beehouses are empty, but only once a Queen has been added.

﻿"[i]Honey Sprite[/i]": Sprite options for Honey; options include Vanilla, [url=https://henrysoftware.itch.io/pixel-food]Henry Software[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5394]Cometkins[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/18359]Gemnour[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/39019]Em[/url], and Harry (that's me!). All sprites used with permission.
﻿"[i]Mead Sprite[/i]": Sprite options for Mead; options include Vanilla, Cometkins, Gemnour, Em, and Harry.
﻿"[i]Bee House Sprites[/i]": Default true. The custom bee house sprites added by this mod can be turned off in case you prefer to use a recolor from another mod.  Turning this off means there will be no variation of the bee house between different kinds of bees. In order to add your own sprites for the bee house variations, see Retexture Mod  Compatibility below.
﻿"[i]Bee House Style[/i]": Additional options for the Bee House sprites, includes Vanilla colors, Desaturated colors, and Medieval. Default Vanilla.

[b]Retexture Mod Compatibility[/b]
This mod retextures the bee house with a series of alternate colors that change based on location and the player's chosen bees. If you're a retexture artist who would like to add your own take on these alternate bee house designs, I've included an optional file called MurmurOfBeesAlternateSpriteTemplate that has set up the conditions necessary for changing the bee houses to match this mod. Feel free to use this in your own retexture mod! [b]Remember[/b], the config option "[i]Bee House Sprites[/i]" on this mod will need to be set to false.

[b]Compatibility[/b]
﻿Because revitalizing the bees has been a fairly common mod idea, efforts have been made to integrate this mod with existing bee expansion mods, or at least make sure they're compatible.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/30597]﻿Bees Plus[/url] and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/24842]Cornucopia[/url]; as mentioned above, both mods are fully integrated with this mod, either individually or at the same time. Beeswax from both mods can be produced by most bees in this mod, while Dried Flowers from Cornucopia can be produced by Mason Bees. Royal Jelly from Cornucopia can also be produced as a byproduct of flower honey by the Honey Bees, Bumblebees, and Island Bees, but not the the Wasps or Mason Bees. Wild Bees technically can [i]if[/i] you have another mod that allows flowers to be grown outside the farm.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/22848]﻿Better Honey Mead[/url] is also compatible; my mod changes the texture for Honey in order to make it a colored item, though this primarily goes into effect on the Wasp Honey and Island Honey in order to keep them from stacking with other types of honey. Better Honey Mead also makes honey a colored item, and has priority over this mod. Wasp and Island Honey still get the color assigned to them by this mod, though using the colored label sprite from Better Honey Mead. Turning off colored sprites in the BHM config will result in no honey or mead being colored either by BHM or this mod.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/30945]﻿Colored Honey Labels[/url], pretty much the same thing as Better Honey Mead.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/39814]﻿Simple Flower Mead[/url] is compatible; my mod will still apply the color overlay for honey and mead sprites, while SFM will keep the name of the flower used to flavor mead. Neither BHM nor SFM can display mead made from Wasp Honey as Wasp Mead, unfortunately.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/10996]﻿Better Beehouses[/url]: Full compatibility, I believe. All the Better Beehouses features I tested work, including alternate honey sources, flower boost, optional quality and bear boost quality, and of course the animated bees. Better Beehouses can add quality to any honey, but leaving Quality unchecked in Better Beehouses still results in quality boosted honey from the Bumblebees. Similarly, changing Better Beehouses' DaysToProduce changes the days between production on all bee types, but if you leave it at 4 (or return it to 4 after having changed it) the Honey Bees still produce faster (and Wasps still produce slower).
﻿Bees in the Greenhouse count as bees on the farm and will match your current type of bee; they will still only produce items if you use Better Beehouses to work indoors. Similarly, with Better Beehouses installed, the Wasps will grant their farming buffs inside the Greenhouse, though this can be turned off in the config file if you are not playing with beehouses working in the Greenhouse.
﻿For the sake of balance, I would recommend leaving the Quality off and the DaysToProduce at 4 because my bees specifically boost one of those things at a time, but hey, if you want daily iridium-star quality honey, you do you.
﻿[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/26321]Honey Extend[/url] and other mods that add new Bee Houses. My mod only effects the vanilla Bee House, so mods like Honey Extend which only make a new type of Bee House and do not change the vanilla Bee House are compatible.  Mods that change the output rules of the vanilla Bee House will likely cause interference.
﻿Mods that change the textures of Craftables or Objects; there may be interference. My mod replaces the texture of the Bee House, Honey, and (optionally) Mead; my changes to the Bee House persisted over [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5513]Gwen's Medieval Craftables[/url], for instance, but Better Honey Mead's changes to the Honey sprite were prioritized over mine. Which mod 'wins' in any given instance likely depends on the methods used by each mod.
﻿[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/20054]Vanilla Plus Professions[/url]﻿ is mostly compatible, with one known issue; two of the talents introduced in the Farming talent tree affect bee houses; [b]Harmonious Blooming[/b], which allows bee houses to produce extra honey based on the number of flowers in range, works perfectly fine (and affects the amount of non-honey items produced as well). [b]Abundance[/b], which allows honey to gain quality when left unharvested overnight, has issues; instead, it's randomly assigning quality to items produced on day one and does not change when the items are left unharvested. Unlocking the talent and then disabling it in the talent tree menu fixes the issue and the bee houses work as intended by this mod.  Otherwise, there are no errors or issues by using both mods.
﻿[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/24355]Walk of Life[/url] is compatible, with the Producer and Yieldmeister professions proportionately increasing the speed at which different types of bees produce (Yieldmeister, for instance, makes Honey Bees produce every day, while Wasps produce every 3). If this feels unbalanced, the easy solution is to exclude bees from animals in the Walk of Life config. (Thank you Pepsiman for testing this one!)
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/3753]﻿Stardew Valley Expanded[/url] and other mods that add new areas to the Farm: the code allows me to add certain locations that are intended to be extensions of the Farm so that the Farm Hive and all the choices and upgrades made with it, will count on those extra locations. These can be added based on whether or not players have specific mods; at the moment, if you have Better Beehouses, the Greenhouse counts and if you have the Ferngill Frontier Farm of Stardew Valley Expanded, the Frontier itself counts.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/22256]﻿Extra Machine Configs[/url] is not required, but does affect the Dried Flowers produced by Mason Bees. With EMC, Dried Flowers become dried versions of blooming nearby flowers and their price is adjusted to match, much like the vanilla honey.
